## Trial `local-package-repository-rhel7__cQtQUgM`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: a local repository was built and served via httpd on node1, remote repos were verifiably blocked with iptables while the local repo remained reachable, and the tree package was installed strictly from the local repo during that disruption. Connectivity was restored afterward, and the mandatory restart protocol shows a clean pre-restart baseline, a real reboot (boot id changed, cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and full post-restart recovery of httpd, the repo, the installed package, and connectivity.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.900 | 26/1 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **local-repo-served — Satisfied:** Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
  - **Why:** createrepo/yum-utils/httpd installed, tree RPM downloaded into /srv/localrepo, createrepo generated repodata, files copied to /var/www/html/localrepo, httpd started (active+enabled), and repomd.xml returned HTTP 200 from http://$NODE_IP/localrepo/. Confirmed again post-restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2db0fe4688754ce5`, `cmd-81bc6185c0d04f4d`, `cmd-799906d0ebf040ab`, `cmd-4c9e7b69c66e4dd6`, `cmd-691e5680fe6c42c8`, `cmd-f021f91303d146a0`
- **remote-unreachable — Satisfied:** Make usual remote repositories unreachable while performing the install
  - **Why:** iptables OUTPUT rules were added to REJECT outbound 80/443 except to node IP/localhost; direct verification shows the remote vault mirror fails (curl exit 7, code 000) while the local repo still returns HTTP 200 at the same moment.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5d0dc5c309fc4440`, `cmd-af70ad1c78e543f7`
- **install-from-local — Satisfied:** Install a package from the local repository while remotes are unreachable
  - **Why:** With remote destinations blocked, yum install of tree was restricted to --enablerepo=local-repo and succeeded; rpm -q and yum list installed both confirm the package is present and sourced from @local-repo.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-889f0e6c302b4da8`, `cmd-51c90b9e72ee4ebc`
- **restart-evidence — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovered state)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart baseline (boot_id 3dba43a5..., httpd active/enabled, repo HTTP 200, tree installed) was captured, a detached reboot returned an ack before disconnect, SSH went unreachable during the transition, and a new boot_id (9a21a3eb...) was observed on reconnect. Post-restart checks confirm httpd, repo serving, package presence, repo config, clean iptables, and remote connectivity all recovered. This matches the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot (9a21a3eb...), cross-confirming an actual reboot occurred.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-6540452a02124fc4`, `cmd-1542e0726e6241ad`, `cmd-efdd5d78a97f4ea4`, `cmd-2fe95af9ad704af7`, `cmd-dfa1c589ebd04241`, `cmd-f021f91303d146a0`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. State-changing commands are largely well-justified: adding a temporary vault repo and installing createrepo/yum-utils/httpd were necessary prerequisites (network was up at that point, before disruption); building/serving the local repo and installing tree are the core task actions; the iptables block/unblock cycle was bounded and fully reverted (final check shows OUTPUT chain back to default ACCEPT-all in cmd-0212cd7e34164097 and cmd-f021f91303d146a0); the reboot was required by the fixed restart protocol and recovery was verified. Minor residue: the vault.repo file was moved to /root/vault.repo.disabled rather than deleted (cmd-5f3cc1c16d6843c9) — a small, harmless leftover artifact rather than an abandoned or conflicting config, since it was removed from /etc/yum.repos.d and does not affect repo resolution. Two failed iptables attempts (cmd-dc7cfb054158426e, syntax error) made no lasting change and were immediately corrected. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-5f3cc1c16d6843c9`, `cmd-0212cd7e34164097`, `cmd-f021f91303d146a0`, `cmd-dc7cfb054158426e`
